summary: Setup wizard loses database password mid-flow → install connects as root with no password
description:
Symptom
During first-time setup (InitializationFilter), schema creation fails with:
Access denied for user 'root'@'<host>' (using password: NO)
even though a password was entered in the wizard. using password: NO means an empty password reached the JDBC driver; the username is intact. Reproducible with a plain mvn cargo:run and a single browser (no container or concurrency required).
Where the credentials come from
The create-database step authenticates with wizardModel.createDatabaseUsername / createDatabasePassword, passed straight to DriverManager.getConnection (InitializationFilter lines 1430–1431 → 1208). Their defaults are createDatabaseUsername = "root" and createDatabasePassword = "" (InitializationWizardModel lines 130, 140). The observed error is exactly these defaults with the password never overridden — i.e. the entered password was present, then lost.
Root cause (three interacting facts)
`wizardModel` is a process-wide singleton, created once in InitializationFilter.init() (line 1120) and shared across all requests/sessions.

Password fields are deliberately excluded from session state. SessionModelUtils skips any field whose name contains password in both saveToSession (line 48) and loadFromSession (line 80). Every non-password field round-trips through the session (saveToSession at end of doPost line 866; loadFromSession at start of doGet line 221), so it survives. Passwords live only in the singleton and cannot be restored once cleared.

`clearPasswords()` fires on every parameterless GET to the setup page. doGet lines 274–279: when page == null, it calls clearPasswords() (line 413), blanking createDatabasePassword, databaseRootPassword, etc.

Net effect: any page == null GET wipes the shared in-memory password while the username and all flags survive via the session — producing root + empty password.
Why a parameterless GET happens routinely
StartupFilter.doFilter lines 182–185 redirect any request that isn't /initialsetup//autorunopenmrs (and isn't an /images or /initfilter/scripts asset) to /openmrs/initialsetup with no query string. The browser follows that 302 with GET /openmrs/initialsetup → page == null → clearPasswords(). A favicon.ico request, a stray asset, a refresh, or Back mid-wizard is enough. The install itself runs in a background thread that reads wizardModel.createDatabasePassword live at task-execution time, so a wipe any time between entry and execution is fatal.
Notes / scope
The form validates a non-empty password on entry (advanced path line 614; simple path line 534), so this is purely a "lost after entry" problem, not bad input.

Affects the interactive UI paths (simple and advanced). The TESTING and "current database user" paths use currentDatabasePassword, which has the same session-exclusion exposure.

Possible directions (for discussion, not decided)
Snapshot the needed credentials into the background install job at start, and stop clearPasswords() from firing on incidental parameterless GETs (keeps passwords out of the session).

Persist passwords in the session for the setup duration and clear them explicitly on completion/abort (puts credentials in session memory — the thing currently avoided).

Make the entire wizard model session-scoped instead of a shared singleton.
